scope: 10 original Nintendo 64 titles; 21 selected published screenshots. No AI images or downloaded ROMs.
method: Public image bytes retained unchanged; hashes checked. Contact sheet and HTML sizing are derivatives. Published images mix native-sized, upscaled, unknown-emulator and official-emulation captures; no exact native pixel budgets inferred from unknown pipelines. All observations are visual analysis of stills; no gameplay video or motion timing was inspected.

screenshots.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

original_release.note: Release date describes this original N64 title in the stated region, not necessarily capture region.

screenshots.credit: Zelda Temple screenshot gallery; copyright Nintendo. Individual capture author unnamed.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 320×240 PNG served by gallery resize URL; image bytes are retained unchanged. N64-specific gallery; hardware, VI and emulator pipeline unstated.
screenshots.observations: Market NPCs differ in body width, height, skirt length, shoulders, hair and sleeves. Long bright dress masses remain distinct when eyes disappear. Link’s green cap/tunic and brown boot/leg break read against the stone street; rear-view identity cannot depend on eyes.

screenshots.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

original_release.note: Release date describes this original N64 title in the stated region, not necessarily capture region.

screenshots.credit: Zelda Temple screenshot gallery; copyright Nintendo. Individual capture author unnamed.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 320×240 PNG; N64-specific gallery, capture hardware/VI/emulator unstated. Shop close-up, not normal traversal size.
screenshots.observations: The shopkeeper uses enormous forearms/hands, wide shoulders, dark beard and a small head relative to his chest. Heavy brow and beard provide an adult expression without childlike eyes. Camera placement makes the face readable while retaining a strong body design.

original_release.note: Release date describes this original N64 title in the stated region, not necessarily capture region.

screenshots.capture_note: Published 320×240 PNG; N64-specific gallery. Capture hardware/VI/emulator unstated. Original N64 game, not Majora’s Mask 3D.
screenshots.observations: A small Link is readable through cap, shield, tunic and visible boot shapes, not small face features. The relatively low traversal camera exposes head and torso contours. Brown/green outfit masses remain coherent rather than fragmenting into many equal-contrast details.

screenshots.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask

original_release.note: Release date describes this original N64 title in the stated region, not necessarily capture region.

screenshots.credit: Zelda Temple screenshot gallery; copyright Nintendo. Individual capture author unnamed.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 320×240 PNG; N64-specific gallery; pipeline unstated. Original N64 shop conversation, not a 3DS remake or flat portrait.
screenshots.observations: The conversation subject’s green hair, pale shirt, modest eye marks and forward-leaning body/arms create a distinct NPC. The conversation camera brings the face forward while keeping Link in frame. Hair and shoulders carry identity; expression does not require every person to share Goemon-size eyes.

screenshots.title: Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon

original_release.note: Release date describes this original N64 title in the stated region, not necessarily capture region.

screenshots.observations: Yae’s large eyes and brows dominate; nose and mouth stay tiny. Angular green bangs leave a broad exposed face window and continue into long side hair. Purple collar frames the chin. Hair has a few deliberate large points, with no fine strands needed.

screenshots.title: Goemon's Great Adventure

original_release.note: Original N64 sequel. North America and Europe listed as 1999. Screenshot uses English dialogue, with exact English release region unstated.

screenshots.credit: Nintendo Life screenshot gallery (individual capture author not named); game copyright Konami.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 640×478 JPEG from the gallery’s original linked large.jpg asset, retained unchanged. Capture hardware/emulator, internal resolution, filtering and scaling are unstated. Original N64 game presentation; do not derive native eye-pixel counts from these published files.
screenshots.observations: Front-on dialogue composition, actual polygon characters. Goemon has an exceptionally large spiky hair volume, huge blue/white eyes, a tiny mouth, small triangle nose and dark brows. Ebisumaru has a large projecting nose, curved brow/eyelid marks and a wide round head. Both use simple chunky hands, short limbs, wide shoe shapes, a single dominant clothing color and a few contrasting trims. This close camera reveals patterned sleeves without making them the primary identification cue.

screenshots.title: Goemon's Great Adventure

screenshots.capture_note: Published 577×445 JPEG from the gallery’s original linked large.jpg asset, retained unchanged. Capture hardware/emulator, internal resolution, filtering and scaling are unstated. Original N64 game presentation; do not derive native eye-pixel counts from these published files.
screenshots.observations: In a shop interior, Goemon remains distinct through the huge blue starburst hair and red outfit with yellow edging. At the smaller gameplay size the eyes still form two light/dark marks, while mouth and fabric details contribute little. Thick wrists and hands separate from the red torso; white shoes anchor the legs. The NPC behind the counter is recognized through a black hair mass, pale face and magenta clothing blocks.

screenshots.title: Quest 64

original_release.note: Release date describes this original N64 title in the stated region, not necessarily capture region.

screenshots.title: Doubutsu no Mori (Animal Forest)

original_release.note: Original Japanese N64 game, not the GameCube Animal Crossing release.

screenshots.credit: Nookipedia: current upload AlexBot2004, 2020-11-30; original upload LoneShadowStar, 2018-01-08. Game copyright Nintendo.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 319×237 PNG; uploader comment says “Native resolution, daytime”. This is source metadata, not independently established capture hardware/VI. Nookipedia marks it specifically Doubutsu no Mori.
screenshots.observations: Large round head and cap silhouette, two prominent eye marks, very short torso, thick short legs, mitten-like hands, and bright shoe tips. Head turns enough toward the overhead camera to keep the face visible. Clothing is a few high-contrast regions rather than small folds. Compact proportions suit a social map camera.

screenshots.title: Doubutsu no Mori (Animal Forest)

original_release.note: Original Japanese N64 game, not the GameCube Animal Crossing release.

screenshots.credit: Nookipedia: Vmario97, 2019-04-24. Game copyright Nintendo.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 640×480 PNG. Original N64 game provenance comes from the file description and DnM-exclusive gallery; capture hardware, internal resolution and rescaling are unstated. No closer conversation capture secured.
screenshots.observations: Player wears a tall cone cap and yellow/red shirt. Large simple dark eyes dominate the face; facial skin is an uninterrupted readable plane beneath the hat. Short arms separate from the torso, feet spread enough for a clear stance. Static is distinguished immediately by huge ears/tail, purple head mass and lightning marking. One silhouette feature can do more than extra facial lines.

screenshots.title: Mega Man 64

original_release.note: N64 version release; Nintendo Life and GameFAQs both give January 10. Legends Station gives January 16, so day-level secondary-source disagreement exists. No original N64 publisher release page was found.

screenshots.credit: Nintendo64EVER N64 screenshot collection. Individual capture author not named. Game copyright Capcom.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 640×480 PNG. N64-only gallery includes Mega Man 64 title-screen evidence. Capture device, emulator, filtering and internal/rendered resolution unstated; not PS1 Legends gallery.
screenshots.observations: Mega Man is readable from behind through bright blue torso, distinct dark-blue boots, square shoulder pads and a strong dark hair mass. Boots and forearms are oversized relative to limbs. Large contiguous color blocks and dark joint breaks preserve a coherent whole against the green field; the face contributes nothing in the normal rear view.

screenshots.title: Mega Man 64

original_release.note: N64 version release; Nintendo Life and GameFAQs both give January 10. Legends Station gives January 16, so day-level secondary-source disagreement exists. No original N64 publisher release page was found.

screenshots.credit: Nintendo64EVER N64 screenshot collection. Individual capture author not named. Game copyright Capcom.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 640×480 PNG. Capture pipeline and scaling unstated. This is a somewhat larger side-on gameplay view, NOT a dedicated face close-up; no confidently N64-specific close face capture secured.
screenshots.observations: Chunky boots project forward, knees are separated, large shoulder/forearm forms create a clear profile, and hair sits as one strong volume atop the light face. Dark outlines on armor panels are restrained compared with the broad blue areas. Weight and pose read from the body even where the side face is tiny.

screenshots.title: Harvest Moon 64

original_release.note: Official Nintendo Japanese release list. Screens below are English-language release captures, whose precise release region is not identified by the gallery.

screenshots.credit: RPGFan screenshot gallery; game copyright Victor Interactive Software/Natsume. Individual screenshot author not named.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 905×680 WebP (gallery display markup says 640×480). Capture device/emulator/filtering and scaling are not stated. Small character figures are sprites in a polygonal-looking environment; do not treat them as runtime polygon heads.
screenshots.observations: Group outside the church: characters stay distinct through hat/hair outline, long-vs-short clothing masses, broad bright palettes, and conspicuous shoes. Head occupies a large share of each tiny body; separate feet and a rounded mitten-like hand read more clearly than fingers. Faces do not carry the entire identity.

original_release.note: Official Nintendo Japanese release list. Screens below are English-language release captures, whose precise release region is not identified by the gallery.

screenshots.credit: RPGFan screenshot gallery; game copyright Victor Interactive Software/Natsume. Individual screenshot author not named.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 905×680 WebP (gallery display markup says 640×480); capture pipeline/scaling unstated. Separate illustrated portrait in the dialogue box, NOT a polygon close-up. In-world figures are sprites.
screenshots.observations: Rick conversation: wide hat brim, strong hair mass, white apron/shirt and green trousers form a readable sprite at distance. Dialogue portrait uses very large eyes, brows and mouth while the map figure keeps only minimal face marks. A portrait can provide emotional detail without bloating every map head.

screenshots.title: Pokémon Snap

original_release.note: Original N64 game release. Screens below are later captures of the original game; one is explicitly Switch Nintendo 64 emulation.

screenshots.credit: GameGrin, Bex Prouse, 2024-03-26. Game copyright Nintendo/Creatures/Game Freak/HAL Laboratory.
screenshots.capture_note: 1280×720 original uploaded JPEG, with pillarbox borders. Article explicitly says the author played the Nintendo 64 emulator on Switch. Original N64 game presentation via later official emulation, NOT native-hardware output and NOT New Pokémon Snap. Do not infer 320×240 feature budgets from it.
screenshots.observations: Todd in ZERO-ONE during intro: polygon head with a single clear auburn hair cap, broad purple/pink shirt stripes, thick short sleeves, simple skin-color hand shapes. Body lean and wide arm gesture communicate action despite a rigid simple mesh; camera and vehicle obscure the lower body. This view is a body/pose comparison, not face evidence.

screenshots.title: Pokémon Snap

original_release.note: Original N64 game release. Screens below are later captures of the original game; one is explicitly Switch Nintendo 64 emulation.

screenshots.credit: Pokémon France original Pokémon Snap gallery. Game copyright Nintendo/Creatures/Game Freak/HAL Laboratory.
screenshots.capture_note: Published French-language 400×300 JPEG. Capture hardware, emulation and rescaling unstated. Oak is flat portrait artwork in a menu, NOT a freely walking polygon NPC. Other gallery art of Todd and Oak was rejected as promotional illustration.
screenshots.observations: Oak’s face is deliberately large in the frame: angular brows, open white eye shapes, broad mouth, bold hair edge and dark facial outlines. White coat frames the face and red shirt separates chest from skin. His identity survives through strong graphic shapes; the original Snap interface is a useful menu/portrait contrast, not a direct polygon face template.

screenshots.title: Hybrid Heaven

original_release.note: Original N64 title; English screenshots have unspecified capture region.

screenshots.credit: Nintendo Life screenshot gallery (individual capture author not named); game copyright Konami.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 576×448 JPEG from the gallery’s original linked large.jpg asset, retained unchanged. Capture hardware/emulator, internal resolution, filtering and scaling are unstated. Original N64 game presentation; do not derive native eye-pixel counts from these published files.
screenshots.observations: Normal corridor view shows a much more realistic body/head ratio than Goemon or Animal Forest. Blue trouser legs, a broad brown jacket/back, blond hair and a stable dark gap between the legs identify the character at distance. The hands are small and the face is turned away, so their fine detail cannot help. Long limbs and narrow head trade immediate toy-like readability for a more adult action-adventure tone.

screenshots.title: Hybrid Heaven

original_release.note: Original N64 title; English screenshots have unspecified capture region.

screenshots.credit: Nintendo Life screenshot gallery (individual capture author not named); game copyright Konami.
screenshots.capture_note: Published 575×447 JPEG from the gallery’s original linked large.jpg asset, retained unchanged. Capture hardware/emulator, internal resolution, filtering and scaling are unstated. Original N64 game presentation; do not derive native eye-pixel counts from these published files.
screenshots.observations: Close polygon cutscene with realistic textured male faces: brows, eye sockets, nose highlight/shadow and mouth are concentrated in the texture. Head outline remains faceted; muted shaded colors produce a more photographic appearance. Suit color and a bright tie identify bodies, but face texture detail depends heavily on this close framing. This is a useful contrast, not a recommendation to copy photographic shading onto small friendly map characters.

screenshots.observations: Optional supporting image: full-body polygon characters in a cutscene, not the ordinary gameplay camera. Narrow shoulders and arms of black-suited guards contrast with the broader jacket and crossed-arm pose of the central character. Trousers form long large uninterrupted regions, shoes are explicit wedge-like volumes, hair is strongly grouped at the head, and hands stay simple rather than individually articulated fingers.
